title: lazyrunner project profile
description: What a project is for lazyrunner: the file that marks its repo, the folder whose changes need a rebuild, and the apps it runs. Schema version 1 (projects/README.md). In a repo's .lazyrunner.json, detect can be left out, and with extends only the changes are needed.

$schema.description: Lets editors check the file; lazyrunner ignores it.

schemaVersion.description: The profile format version. lazyrunner refuses a version it doesn't know.

extends.description: Only in a repo's .lazyrunner.json: the id of a known profile this file changes. Its top-level fields replace that profile's; apps merge by key.

id.description: Short lowercase name. Names the project's settings in lazyrunner.config.json and its state folder.

detect.description: How lazyrunner recognises the repo. Required, except in a repo's .lazyrunner.json (that file marks the repo).

anyFile.description: A file only this project's repo has, relative to its root. lazyrunner looks for it upward from the current folder. One file for now.

watch.description: The folder whose changes need a rebuild of the .NET apps (unchanged builds are skipped; restart on code change). One folder for now.

apps.description: The apps lazyrunner runs, left to right as its columns: .NET apps and npm apps (the tables below).

relativePath.description: Relative to the repo root; / or \ both work.

appKey.description: Lowercase letters and digits, starting with a letter.

icon.description: One character before the app's name in its title bar.

dotnetApp.title: A .NET app ("type": "dotnet")
dotnetApp.description: An ASP.NET (or any dotnet run) project. lazyrunner builds it with dotnet build, one build at a time and skipped when nothing in watch changed, then runs it with dotnet run --no-build --launch-profile.

key.description: Short name, unique in the profile. Used in settings (columnWidths, apps.<key>) and by servedBy.

type.description: The app type: what lazyrunner does with the app follows from it.

launchProfile.description: A profile in the project's Properties/launchSettings.json. Its applicationUrl gives the port.

swagger.description: Optional. The Swagger UI path: lazyrunner probes <swagger>/index.html for the response time, and w opens it. Without it lazyrunner probes /.

tests.description: Optional. Test suites that belong to this app in the tests view (T), whatever lazyrunner works out: .NET test projects by path from the repo root or by name, Nx projects by name. Without it a .NET test project belongs to the app whose project it references, an npm or Nx suite to the npm app whose folder it runs in.

npmApp.title: An npm app ("type": "npm")
npmApp.description: A folder with package.json, run with npm run <script>. It needs no build from lazyrunner; i runs npm ci for it.

key.description: Short name, unique in the profile.

type.description: The app type: what lazyrunner does with the app follows from it.

variants.description: How it runs, chosen again on every start: the first variant whose when.packageScript package.json has. One without when always applies, so only the last can leave it out.

tests.description: Optional. Test suites that belong to this app in the tests view (T), whatever lazyrunner works out: .NET test projects by path from the repo root or by name, Nx projects by name. Without it a .NET test project belongs to the app whose project it references, an npm or Nx suite to the npm app whose folder it runs in.

serveVariant.title: A dev-server variant
serveVariant.description: The script starts a server on a port (vite, ng serve, next dev …). The app is up once the port listens.

label.description: Shown in the column next to the script.

port.description: The dev server's port, unless the script itself says --port <n>.

buildVariant.title: A watch-build variant
buildVariant.description: The script builds and keeps watching, and a .NET app serves the output. The app is up once ready.file is written.

label.description: Shown in the column next to the script.

servedBy.description: The key of the .NET app that serves the build: w opens the app on its port.

file.description: A file the build writes, relative to dir: the app is ready once it is newer than the start.

when.description: When the variant applies; without it, always.

packageScript.description: The variant applies on a checkout whose package.json has this script (so it can differ per branch).
